newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: Aleman, army to disband Nicaraguan gangs jointly.
newsitem.headline: Aleman, army to disband Nicaraguan gangs jointly.

text.p: Nicaragua's new President Arnoldo Aleman met with top army brass on Thursday and said they would coordinate efforts to demobilize armed gangs still operating in northern Nicaragua.
Following a courtesy visit to army chief Gen. Joaquin Cuadra, Aleman said army, civilian and government officials would meet next Tuesday to discuss plans to negotiate the disbanding of the gangs.

"They must understand that the armed struggle, taking up the gun, is no longer appropriate. We are going to offer them the opportunity to integrate into civilian life," Aleman, who took office on Jan. 10, told reporters.

Cuadra said about 500 members of the gangs, some of whom were Contra rebels or from the Sandinista People's Army who re-armed after the 1990 peace treaty, still operated in remote regions of northern Nicaragua. Since Nicaragua's civil war ended in 1990, armed bands have killed 1,000 people, wounded 400 and kidnapped 600 civilians, he said.
Last Thursday an armed band ambushed and killed six soldiers, including three officers, in the central province of Matagalpa.

Tuesday midnight was the deadline given by the government for members of the armed units to assemble in specially designated "peace zones" in the provinces of Matagalpa and Jinotega in preparation for negotiations with the government.

Government officials said about 300 had assembled so far in the zones, in which the rebels were guaranteed safety, food and medicine. Talks were to have begun on Wednesday but the remote terrain where the zones were located meant the start had been delayed, officials said.
